correction_summary: Use build-first bounded tranches with integrated QA and one final hosted gate, and route blocked structured repository writes through the governed semantic bridge instead of repeatedly fighting connector wrappers.
failure_summary: Repeated per-item completion loops, broad validation cycles, prose-sensitive repairs, and repeated connector wrapper retries caused avoidable stalls despite already-governed repository state and known evidence.

evidence: Owner explicitly approved the build-first integrated run pattern as the default for all runs and directed that wrapper handling be simplified.
CAPP-04 through CAPP-12 were completed as one integrated tranche with one final projection.
Efficiency policy v1.1.0 adds the build-first run pattern and single-failure connector routing rule.
Governed write bridge allowlist now includes continuity and correction semantic commands.

proposed_case.name: Blocked governed write routes once to semantic bridge
proposed_case.setup: A repository mutation is owner-authorized, reversible, within an allowlisted governed path, and supported by current repository evidence, but the normal connector mutation is rejected by the platform wrapper without a project-policy defect.
proposed_case.owner_input: Continue the approved bounded run using the established build-first integrated execution pattern.
expected_actions: Attempt the smallest normal connector mutation once.
After one wrapper rejection, use a small typed governed write request when the mutation fits the bridge allowlist.
Preserve read-only final hosted validation and signed merge evidence.
Build and validate the bounded tranche before projecting completion once.
prohibited_actions: Repeatedly reformulate or retry the same large blocked mutation.
Treat platform wrapper rejection as proof that the governed project operation is invalid.
Weaken completion, permission, privacy, provenance, checksum, or release gates.
Create a separate completion-only PR for every item in an approved integrated tranche.
proposed_case.pass_condition: The work advances through the governed semantic path after at most one connector-wrapper rejection, the tranche is validated by one final read-only hosted gate, and completion evidence remains intact without redundant per-item completion loops.
